request.current_synthesis: Observation: T1 training produced a learning trajectory whose recorded training success rose to 0.96, but development evaluation of complete artifacts was only 65.625% and 68.75%; the later artifact won 9 paired episodes versus 4, with 13 discordant episodes. Interpretation: the later checkpoint is the stronger complete artifact at the candidate-comparison level, but the difference is not assigned to training duration or any mechanism. Interpretation: the dominant observed failure class is failure to reach tolerance, not failure to sustain the 100-step hold, because no-first-entry episodes account for most failures and entry generally led to a complete hold. This supports the model consequence that official coverage and learned reach basins matter. The radius-specific contribution and the roles of IK branch, reset singularity, and actuator margin remain unresolved because those diagnostics were not recorded in this evaluation.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved decision is whether the reach deficit is primarily an official inner-radius coverage/generalization problem or a branch/singular-escape/control-authority problem. Radius-stratified outcomes from the existing artifacts or a targeted measurement would support a coverage route if failures concentrate at 6-14 cm; failures distributed by radius with branch or saturation signatures would redirect toward branch-aware control or simulator characterization. Hold diagnostics do not currently justify prioritizing memory or explicit hold phase.
